answer: To keep cheap clones from flooding attestation, every new agent posts a time-locked work bond that three already-final peers must countersign after reviewing a unique execution receipt. When two receipts share a signing kernel, the bond schedule enters a spiral: the second identity pays 4x, the third 16x, and the cluster's stake is slashed if those signers later prove reuse. Proofs travel by a delayed raven courier — a public, append-only path no alias can rewrite — while any established peer may whisper a challenge into the same window. Farms therefore spend faster than they can earn votes.
